content:
For the longest time I've always found the usage of unbundled relations in the docs#Ordinal API to be quite annoying. Mathematically, ordinals are supposed to be equivalence classes of well-orders, but in practice we can't use this characterization very well because the API is stated in the setting of IsWellOrder α r, rather than LinearOrder α + WellFoundedLT α. And this leads to bespoke theorems like docs#Ordinal.bounded_singleton or docs#Cardinal.unbounded_of_unbounded_sUnion which are hard to even parse.

I would like to change the API to one taking bundled well-orders, rather than unbundled ones. I've already taken a first step towards this in #35513, which redefines docs#Order.cof to take in a preorder rather than a reflexive relation, which allows us to use the existing API on docs#IsCofinal (the changed proofs are much nicer now, in my opinion). But my intention is to eventually redefine even ordinals themselves, as a quotient of a type of bundled well-orders, rather than a type of unbundled ones.

I see one potential problem with this: we might want to, under some circumstances, define a well-order on a type that already has an order instance. It's not unheard of to see mathematical arguments start with sentences such as "take a well-ordering of the reals". Though I'd argue that this could be dealt with via a type alias, perhaps something like WellOrder α, which overrides any order structure on α and declares its own LinearOrder + WellFoundedLT instances.

I'm mostly just opening this thread as a sanity check that what I'm doing is desirable, and that no one has any major complaints about the new design.

cc. @Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 @Snir Broshi @Yaël Dillies
@Bhavik Mehta you may also be interested in this , as it touches on your idea for the ordinal/order type refactor.
I would really like to get some feedback on whether this is a good idea. I think @Snir Broshi had some pushback when I suggested this elsewhere.

I had a bit of a wild idea which might make this work out better. Perhaps we can make notation type[r] for the order type of some non < relation? Kind of how we can write IsOpen[t] for a non-canonical topology.
We would hopefully only use this rarely. But we do have some legitimate uses. e.g. the proof of docs#Cardinal.mul_eq_self defines a bespoke well ordering on α × α that isn't the lexicographic one.

Violeta Hernández said:

change the API to one taking bundled well-orders

When you say bundled well-orders, do you mean mathlib's notion of bundled well-orders, like https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/SetTheory/Ordinal/Basic.html#WellOrder? From your example of the reals, it doesn't seem like you are (since picking a different well-ordering of the reals is clean in this setup)
a bundled well order would be LinearOrder + WellFoundedLT
Worth mentioning that docs#WellOrder is an auxiliary definition with no API that only serves to define the ordinals

My proposal with the reals was to define a type alias (which would probably have to be called something different than WellOrder) which endowed them with a well-order of minimal order type. So that we didn't have to deal with unbundled relations.

Violeta Hernández said:

Worth mentioning that docs#WellOrder is an auxiliary definition with no API that only serves to define the ordinals

Right, and so my question is if your proposal is to use that more, in the way that we use LinOrd for OrderType. But it seems like you mean bundled well-order in a way which is different from the mathlib notion

I think I should clarify. By a "bundled well-order" I don't mean a structure which simultaneously contains a relation and a proof that it is a well-order. I mean a well-ordered < relation, in contrast to an arbitrary well-ordered r or anything else.
So for instance, docs#OrderType.type is only defined for bundled relations
I would like for docs#Ordinal.type to be the same
And then the advantage is that we can make use of ≤ and max and min and suprema and infima and successors and all the theorems that come along.

This is a prerequisite if we want to redefine ordinals as a subtype of order types. Unless of course we generalize docs#OrderType.type to something like docs#IsLinearOrder. Which I think is not a great idea.

Violeta Hernández said:

This is a prerequisite if we want to redefine ordinals as a subtype of order types.

I'm not sure if we do want to do this, but agreed. Thanks for clarifying above.

There's at least a few basic constructions on ordinals that generalize to order types. Both have associative sums and products, which distribute over one another on the right, and are monotone on each argument. Both have 0 as a bottom element, and both have a well-defined monotone function onto cardinals.

It'd be nice if we could avoid the duplication.
Monotone? What's the order on order types?
We can lift algebraic structures through injections without explicit subtypes, so I don't think the duplication would be so bad in either case

Aaron Liu said:

Monotone? What's the order on order types?

x ≤ y when x embeds in y

Bhavik Mehta said:

We can lift algebraic structures through injections without explicit subtypes, so I don't think the duplication would be so bad in either case

Fair enough. I do still think it's weird that we have this differing bundling of order types and ordinals, and I'd like to make things consistent.
